analysis.title: Chart Outlook, Edition 41, 15 November 2026
key_insights: Major global indices held key supports through the November 5-6 AI and chip sell-off, so no new index-level SELL signals were triggered. Most US stocks the author covers had already broken support levels flagged in September and October and triggered SELL signals earlier.

The rebound may be temporary. In many indices it could stall at the 61.8% retracement of the October decline and form the right shoulder of a large head-and-shoulders top, with a breakdown possible in Q1 2027. A sharp downturn in November or December is not ruled out.

S&P 500 reached 7653 on November 12, an almost exact 61.8% retracement of the correction from the 7845 high on October 6 to the 7350 low on November 5. Above 7750 and 8000 the outlook turns bullish toward 8300. Below 7250 and 6800 it turns bearish. The author assigns no probabilities and would buy a break above resistance and sell a break below support.

The broad market is stronger than tech. The S&P 500 Equal Weight Index hit a record 9072 on November 5, and its ratio to the cap-weighted S&P 500 is close to an upside breakout that would signal long-term outperformance. The MSCI World Equal Weight Index held support at 4735 because chip stocks carry less weight in it.

Tech and semiconductors remain weak. The SOX is down 38.6% from its June 22 high of 14,655 to a November 5 low of 8997, described as a textbook bubble. A break below 9000 would suggest the bubble could take several years to deflate. The MSCI World IT Index remains in a downtrend and the author would turn bullish only above 1213.

Nvidia has fallen about 30% since the author's sell signal at the break below 215, reaching a low of 148.80 on November 12. The decline has retraced almost 61.8% of the April 2025 to October 2026 rally. A break of that level points to 93-86, near the April 2025 low. Results are due November 17. Resistance sits at 166.70, 171.80 and 180.

On November 5 the S&P 500 fell about 4%, its worst session since April 2025, and the Nasdaq entered correction territory. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell nearly 10% and Nvidia and Broadcom each lost about 9%. On November 6 Korea's Kospi fell as much as 8.6% intraday.

Macro data were strong but inflation is the headwind. US October payrolls rose 165,000, more than twice the expected figure. October CPI rose 0.4% m/m against a 0.3% forecast and core CPI rose 0.3%, both above forecasts. Markets expect another Fed hike in December.

The US 10-year yield is testing 5.15%, the 61.8% retracement of the October decline. The author expects a rise to the October high of 5.365%. A failure at 5.15% would point to 4.94%, 4.82% or 4.61-4.58%.

Switzerland is defensive. The SMI fell 1.14% to 14,796.50 on November 6 but held above 14,500 support. Nestlé, Novartis and Roche are 48.5% of the index. Swiss CPI rose to 1.5% y/y in October from 1.0%, against 1.3% expected, with core at 0.5%. Markets bet on an SNB hike from 0% on December 10. The Swiss 10-year yield could be bottoming, with breaks above 0.6890% and 0.7620% signalling a long-term uptrend.

DAX hit a record 27,002 on November 12 on rotation into banks, industrials and cyclicals after the US midterms and strong Infineon results, but ran into trendline resistance. A break above 27,100 and 27,500 would target 30,000. The author would SELL below 26,150.
OMX 30 may be forming an ending wedge near record levels. The author would SELL below 3,230.

Dollar is testing key resistance against the franc at 0.8430. A break would signal a long-term breakout toward 0.8480, 0.8550, 0.8620 and 0.8900. Euro fell to 1.1019 against the dollar on November 13, and breaks below 1.0950, 1.0880 and 1.0800 would signal further weakness toward 1.0500. EUR/CHF hit 0.9125 on November 6 during a flight into the franc, then recovered.

Gold fell from 4148 on November 9 and is testing support at 3830-3740, the lower line of an uptrend channel intact since 2023. A break targets 3630, 3470, 3390, 3320 and 3150. Escaping the downtrend requires recovery above 4040, 4180 and 4380.

Bitcoin remains at risk unless it recovers above 73.2k, with next supports at 63.2k-61.1k and 48.2k-44.9k. 48.2k is the key long-term support, the 61.8% retracement of the full uptrend from the 2014 low to the 2025 high.

Global trend count: 11 markets in uptrend, 11 in downtrend and 17 flat. Euro Stoxx, CAC 40 and Sensex are close to upgrades to uptrend. Sector weights: overweight financials, consumer discretionary, health care, staples and utilities. Underweight industrials, IT, communication services and materials. Energy neutral.

risk_factors: A rebound that stops at the 61.8% retracement could form the right shoulder of a large head-and-shoulders top, with a breakdown in Q1 2027 and a possible bear market year.
A sharp downturn in November or December cannot be ruled out.
Hot US inflation and a rising 10-year yield near 5.15% with a Fed hike expected in December.
Nvidia results on November 17 after a roughly 30% decline.
Semiconductor bubble deflation if the SOX breaks below 9000.
Gold breaking the 3830-3740 support zone would also break the uptrend channel in place since 2023.
charts_described: S&P 500 chart: decline from the 7845 high on October 6 to 7350 on November 5, rebound to 7653 on November 12, a 61.8% retracement.
SOX chart: decline of 38.6% from 14,655 to 8997, with 9100-9000 a cluster of at least four Fibonacci relationships.
MSCI World Equal Weight Index chart: low 4735 on November 6, high 4890 on November 12, wedge forming since early 2026.
Gold chart: uptrend channel intact since the 2023 low, price testing its lower line at 3830-3740.
Swiss 10-year yield chart: breaks above 0.6890% and 0.7620% would indicate the decline from the 1.6230% December 2022 high has bottomed.
vol_and_positioning: The AI trade was described as crowded. One fund manager quoted said health care was the funding sector for the AI trade and that this is reversing.
Rotation out of AI and chip stocks into defensives (Nestlé, Novartis, Roche) is cited as a reason for the SMI's resilience.
The ratio of the S&P 500 Equal Weight Index to the cap-weighted S&P 500 has risen since the October low and is close to an upside breakout.
geopolitical: US midterm elections cited as a trigger for rotation into banks, industrials and cyclical stocks in Europe.
Falling oil prices cited as a driver of the rebound that gave Wall Street its best day since April.
